thread.title: UPDATE: Why Nov. 1 is the make-or-break day for the stock market

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Why Nov. 1 is the make-or-break day for the stock market
text:
By Nigam Arora
Apple is the only FAANG stock to hold up, but that could change after the company reports quarterly earnings. If Apple falls, it's likely that the market would follow.
Nov. 1 is a make-or-break day for the U.S. stock market.
How so? Let's first build the necessary background by reading "Here are the six things that could ignite a rally in the stock market (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/can-ibms-big-premium-for-red-hat-ignite-a-sustainable-stock-market-rally-2018-10-29)" and "This money-flow chart shows that Amazon and Netflix are in dangerous territory (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-money-flow-chart-shows-that-amazon-and-netflix-are-in-dangerous-territory-2018-10-26)." Here's a chart to get us going.
Chart
Please click here (https://thearorareport.com/chart-analysis-compare-apple-aapl-stock-to-amazon-amzn-stock) for a chart of Apple (AAPL) stock compared with Amazon (AMZN), the First Trust Dow Jones Internet Index Fund ETF (FDN), the Dow Jones Industrial Average , the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQ). Please note the following:
-- Apple stock has held up well against Amazon stock.
-- The most appropriate comparison is of Apple stock to the Internet ETF, which contains popular stocks such as Facebook (FB), Netflix (NFLX) and Twitter (TWTR).
-- Apple stock has also held up well against its suppliers -- Micron Technology (MU), Qualcomm (QCOM) and Qorvo (QRVO).
Read:Everything Apple just announced at its Mac and iPad Pro event (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/everything-apple-just-announced-at-its-mac-and-ipad-event-2018-10-30)
Ask Arora: Nigam Arora answers your questions about investing in stocks, ETFs, bonds, gold and silver, oil and currencies. Have a question? Send it to Nigam Arora (mailto:ask-arora@thearorareport.com).
Apple will report earnings Nov. 1 after the close of trading. The whisper numbers for Apple are higher than the consensus numbers. Stocks move based on the difference between the whisper numbers and the reported numbers.
Apple is the last domino standing. Its FAANG brethren have all crashed, even the mighty Amazon, which has slumped about 25% from all-time highs. Apple's decline is more in line with that of the S&P 500.
Will Apple fall? If it does, watch out below -- but this warning has to be tempered because of the six factors that can ignite a rally. Those factors are listed in the link above.
Money flows
Prudent investors who want an edge and lower their risk find that segmented money flows are the best tool to give them the edge. For months when popular tech stocks were levitating, The Arora Report has been sharing with you that the smart money was consistently selling into the strength while the momo (momentum) crowd was aggressively buying at highly elevated prices.
Interestingly, as popular tech stocks have fallen, the smart money is mostly inactive and at times a light buyer. But the momo crowd is aggressively selling into the drop. The Arora Report had been cautioning against over-concentration in tech when tech was near its highs. For two classic examples, take a look at the charts of AMD (AMD) and Nvidia (NVDA). In both cases, the momo crowd has suffered massive losses but the smart money made out like a bandit.
